speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: The report outlines Singapore's plans to harness artificial intelligence (AI) for the public good, focusing on enhancing AI capabilities, addressing potential risks and fostering a thriving AI ecosystem.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: We need a strategy that aims to make our nation the global leader in selected AI fields.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: Under NAIS 2.0, the Government's main role revolves around enabling an environment for AI to grow and enhancing the efficiency of public agencies.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: While these are important, the Government certainly has the resources and capability to do much more.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: In this AI-driven era, we need the Government to intercede more proactively to create a world-leading AI industry.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: Simply leaving things to the free market may not produce the desired results because of the constraints of our local private sector and our small domestic market.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: It will risk forfeiting some promising economic growth opportunities that AI can bring for our nation.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: Singapore's small population size should not deter us from global AI leadership.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: Historical industrial successes have been built on strategic government interventions, such as Taiwan’s support of TSMC, which played a pivotal role in its journey to becoming a global semiconductor manufacturing juggernaut.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: Today, I will address NAIS 2.0’s AI labour policy and advocate for a strong AI industrial policy so that Singapore can aim for global leadership in selected AI domains.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: Let us begin with the AI labour policy.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: Concerns linger that, as has happened in the past, foreigners may dominate lucrative positions, including leadership positions, leaving Singaporeans with mainly the routine and lower-paying jobs.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: This could impede our citizens’ career advancement alongside the advancing AI landscape.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: NAIS 2.0 has three labour planks: scaling up AI-specific training programmes; scaling up technology and AI talent pipelines; and remaining open to global tech talent.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: I acknowledge the importance of global AI talent.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: However, there must be a clear differentiation between exceptional global talent and the average foreign technological worker.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: We should welcome the former, but, should avoid importing too many of the latter, as they may end up competing with Singaporeans who can do the job just as well.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: Any global talent that we bring in, must be expected to transfer their skills to locals, not just use Singapore as a springboard for greater pursuits in other countries.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: This can be done through tying company grants to the achievement of knowledge transfer or through limited-term foreign work passes, tied to the training of Singaporean workers.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: The AI playground is level, with a highly collaborative open-source community.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: The core techniques and frameworks are mature enough and reasonably accessible through papers and code.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: With the right training, mentorship and opportunities, Singaporean talent can deliver as well as anyone in the world.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: To raise a body of local AI talent, AI-training programme places and talent pipelines must be focused on Singaporeans.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: We need to plan ahead and start training all our students early in AI – not just students who are academically strong in the sciences and mathematics.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: For mid-career workers, hands-on interaction with AI tools is one of the best forms of training.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: The Government should expand the scope of SkillsFuture Credits, to cover expenses for subscriptions to AI assistants like ChatGPT Plus or Github Co-pilot to accelerate their productivity.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: This will level the playing field for Singaporeans with less means to pay for such subscriptions.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: Paid models like ChatGPT-4, have been assessed to be significantly better than their free counterparts and we should give our workers more opportunities to use the best models.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: It was once unclear if it were possible for humans to reach the moon.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: But US President John F Kennedy made a speech to Congress in 1961, rallying his nation to achieve the goal of landing a man on the moon and returning him safely to Earth before the end of that decade.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: And the National Aeronautics and Space Administration (NASA)'s Apollo 11 mission achieved it ahead of schedule, on 20 July 1969.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: The Government has the resources and capability to take more risks, on a longer timescale, to pursue high-reward moonshots.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: But first, the Government must catch the vision and have the determination to make our country number one in our chosen AI domains.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: Achieving some of these AI moonshots has implications on our economic security and even our sovereignty.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: Advances in AI rely on large, high-quality data sets.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: We must ensure that foreign technological firms and governments do not end up extracting our data overseas to build AI products, which then get sold back to Singaporeans.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: This will allow such firms to profit immensely, while local expertise flounders.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: Currently, no global framework governs cross-border data flows and ownership.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: This allows predatory dynamics to continue between countries and companies.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: Once market dominance is achieved, network effects and the dynamics of chasing a moving target, make it almost impossible for new entrants to catch up.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: If we are not careful, Singapore may become only a consumer of such platforms, while the economic benefits and the best jobs go overseas.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: Singapore should avoid this, by proactively building comprehensive local data sets for homegrown AI development.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: We should pursue a few ambitious, publicly-funded moonshot projects.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: These projects must prioritise transparency and align their outcomes with the national interest, ensuring that economic gains directly benefit our citizens.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: It should be independently run with commercial dynamism, yet be ultimately answerable to Singaporeans.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: Healthcare AI could be a moonshot that Singapore can aim for.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: I will present the case for this and answer the five questions in reverse order.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: Healthcare systems worldwide are under strain, due to ageing populations and chronic disease burdens.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: Healthcare institutions tend to treat diseases late in their course, when symptoms are severe and care is expensive.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: Yet, major conditions like obesity, heart disease and cancer, are driven by shared underlying factors.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: This outdated care model no longer aligns well with scientific reality.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: Healthcare AI, supported by population-scale data, has the potential to predict risks and intervene early to significantly improve health outcomes.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: This will require a reorganisation of healthcare delivery that focuses on early prevention and action.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: Singapore has started this journey through the Healthier SG programme.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: Second, is there a genuine unmet global market gap?

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: Electronic health record (EHR) systems remain fragmented worldwide.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: Even in the US, no dominant player exists in healthcare AI.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: The players are fragmented among various entities, like EHR providers, tech firms, life sciences companies, insurers and hospitals.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: Those with vast healthcare data may not have efficient AI models and vice-versa.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: We can more easily overcome the coordination challenges that may oblige larger ecosystems to build healthcare AI components in a piecemeal fashion.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: So, the Government is already collecting and coordinating healthcare data.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: What is missing, is the impetus to use this data to drive the future of AI through an industrial policy.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: Third, are there "moats" against global technological giants?

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: Healthcare AI depends a lot on having local healthcare teams and physical sensors to collect and manage clinical data.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: AI can serve as an assistant to local healthcare workers and give Singapore an edge over others.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: Singapore has already signalled this commitment to generating comprehensive data, like in the SG100K genome study.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: Healthcare also has more durable data moats over other AI spheres, like linguistics, where SEA-LION's defences against global technological giants in low-resource languages is uncertain.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: Yes, as a public good, healthcare AI can benefit other countries, while facing fewer sovereignty concerns.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: Debates are taking place globally about where large AI systems are trained and deployed.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: However AI, when used for healthcare, which can potentially benefit everyone, is less likely to attract controversies or nationalist and protectionist tendencies.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: By assuming a leadership role in this field, Singapore can export our healthcare AI innovations, generate much international goodwill and even use this to advance our foreign policy.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: Yes, through improved public health, economic growth and global technological leadership.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: Singapore has other comparative advantages in the race for global leadership in healthcare AI.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: We have a robust healthcare system, the SingPass digital ID, cross-domain talent and a history of Government investments and interventions in specific industries.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: Singapore's demographic diversity provides rich healthcare data across ethnicities and ages.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: Healthcare AI can catalyse the development of adjacent fields like computational genomics and precision medicine.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: Singapore has the ingredients for a breakthrough in Healthcare AI.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: To succeed, the Government needs to take the lead in putting these ingredients together.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: To realise a healthcare AI moonshot, Singapore must combine existing ingredients into a coherent strategy.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: We should aim to radically improve our ability to prevent disease, intervene and make causal inferences.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: A multi-modal healthcare AI foundation model, moves beyond narrowly specified point solutions.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: By having a single foundation model for, say, both chest X-rays and retinal image interpretation, we can overcome data fragmentation across medical specialties and make it increasingly possible to uncover foundational principles of diseases.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: We should create comprehensive longitudinal patient histories, spanning years.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: Existing data needs to be sufficiently standardised to serve AI analysis, without a massive amount of preprocessing.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: This will enable large-scale analysis to identify at-risk groups, conduct preventative screening and perform early treatment.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: It will also enable high-quality acute care, as a simultaneous expert in genomics, biology, general medicine and the specialties.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: This could establish an unmatched resource – built in Singapore, for the world.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: Local AI startups can also benefit from this foundation model, to build their own applications to sell to the world.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: It is a proactive strategy to ensure Singapore thrives in the AI-driven future to benefit all Singaporeans.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: I presented just one example of a moonshot that Singapore could pursue.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: There may be other moonshots of equal or greater merit.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: I welcome open debate on selecting moonshots, but, we cannot pull our punches if AI is truly the new industrial revolution.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: Singapore possesses the talent, resources and infrastructure needed to compete for the top spot in selected AI fields.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: Achieving it requires political will, a readiness to embrace risks and proactive intervention by the Government.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: We can do it and we must do it, for the benefit of Singapore and Singaporeans.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: I would encourage the Member to read the many other documents that we have written, which describe how we are already doing many of the things the Member has listed in his speech.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: And, I thank him in advance, for supporting the investments that we plan to make to deliver the various outcomes that he has detailed.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: We have made some of the same points in the past.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: How we approach AI development should result in better jobs for Singaporeans, we agree.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Our approach should lead to skills development and knowledge transfer to Singaporeans and Singapore, we agree.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Ambitious, innovative projects should be attempted to create opportunities, AI can be transformative for healthcare and our small size as a nation should not deter us from seeking excellence and potentially global leadership in AI, we agree with all this, we have said all this before.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: And I am glad that he thinks we should do this.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: But how we do so and how we proceed, matters.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: I will point out that in talking through the mechanisms and the suggestions that Mr Giam has made, his speech does have some internal contradictions.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Statements that he makes to support one strategy, perhaps contracts another.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: He talks about the constraints of our local private sector and our small domestic market, but he wants to suggest exactly doing that in restricting the development of an AI system within Singapore.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: He talks about how there is no global cross-border framework around data sharing, but he wants to worsen that by suggesting data localisation and sovereignty strategies.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: At one part of his speech, he talks about how there is a level playing field for AI with a highly collaborative open source community and then later on, he worries about how there is market dominance and network effects that would make it hard for us to penetrate the market.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: He has differing views, depending on the differing recommendations.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Our approach should target excellence in key domains and create an environment with solid foundations that maximise our chances of success.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: We should not seek global leadership just for the sake of it.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: But let me just recap on a few ideas.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: The strategy focuses on harnessing AI for the public good for Singapore and the world.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: It outlines key enablers and actions that Singapore will take in the coming years to achieve the twin goals of excellence, developing peaks of excellence in AI, including to address the needs and challenges of our time, such as climate change and population health.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Our approach is for AI to have widespread and positive impact on our economy and our society.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: That is why we will develop peaks of excellence across domains, across our economy, selected on the probability to deliver an outsized impact to Singapore and the lives of Singaporeans, including leading economic sectors such as manufacturing and financial services, those relevant to Singapore's smart nation priorities, healthcare and education.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: We already use datasets across various healthcare registries and databases to train AI models, and these are already being piloted for use in clinics across Singapore.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: SingHealth, together with the Ministry of Health (MOH), A*STAR and the National Supercomputing Centre recently organised the AI Health Summit 2023.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: It featured local and international experts discussing the application of advanced AI in healthcare, and it demonstrated many of the projects that are already in development here in Singapore.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Across our society, we will address peaks of excellence for AI.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: We will anchor integrated and transformative AI innovation and value creation activities here, working with companies to base their AI Centres of Excellence, to build new products, develop intellectual property across the AI stack here in Singapore.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Creating this environment for many projects, many peaks of excellence, has two key benefits.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: One is that it makes it more likely that we benefit all either through economic opportunity by being part of the industry or as a beneficiary of the new service.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: The second key benefit is that not all projects are successful.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: With moonshots, Mr Giam will know that outcomes are inherently uncertain and the original moonshot certainly did not have a friction free path to success.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: They are not always clear, and even with the best efforts we may not get the desired or expected results.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: So as we embark on ambitious and innovative projects, I hope we can count on Mr Giam's support to still stand in support of us having made the attempt in the spirit of a moonshot even when it does not quite work out in the way we expect.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: So, trying several different ideas, creating the opportunity for innovation and inventiveness, rather than trying to pick symbolic projects, is far more likely to generate a success.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Anchoring AI activities is only one part of the picture.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: A strong AI ecosystem also requires skilled AI practitioners.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: We want to grow a pool of such high value and skilled jobs here in Singapore.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: As discussed extensively in this House, including by Dr Tan Wu Meng on behalf of his Clementi residents and I think representing the concerns of residents across Singapore in successive Budget speeches, the 2023 Presidential Address Debate, Parliamentary Questions, our recent Parliamentary Motion.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: None of this will become a reality if we do not train, upskill and reskill our labour force.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: That point has been made and the Government's key focus is thus on training our people.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: This will allow Singaporeans to capture new opportunities and shape their future.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: We have also started work on equipping our students with skills relevant to artificial intelligence.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: The Ministry of Education develops students foundational knowledge of AI and promotes its safe and responsible use in schools.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: That said, it is important to recognise that global AI talent plays a complementary role.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: They serve as a bridge to expertise, perspectives, innovative approaches elsewhere that are crucial for the information exchange and skills transfer to strengthen our ecosystem.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Today, we are already experiencing strong demand for AI talent here in Singapore.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Given the fierce competition for this talent globally, it would be quite unwise to limit the pool of skilled practitioners we can draw from and potentially hindering our ecosystem growth.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: There are some other essential enablers that we need here.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: We have to have sufficient compute power so that industry, academia and the Government can innovate, build and deploy high value solutions.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Our strategy on data is important in advancing our AI aspirations.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Our approach on data is premised on supporting innovation, serving the public good and making sure that relevant safeguards are in place.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: We focus on improving the quality of data sets, building up our capability and ensuring that data use for AI development is aligned with trusted data sharing frameworks.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: But domestic data and local AI models are not enough for Singapore to achieve our ambitions.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: But instead, we need to remain connected, allow for and advocate for cross-border data flows as long as adequate protection is ensured.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Recent legislation in large countries avoid this idea of explicit localisation provisions.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Even with their large markets and large data sets, they recognise the benefits of being connected to the world.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: And we benefit from openness and connectivity to the world for our partners to share with us in good faith, and they are less likely to do so if we close ourselves off.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Singapore has thrived as part of a connected world.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: It is the nature of the tech and digital space that Government cannot pick winners and certainly cannot centrally plan their way to success.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: There is also the issue of the cost associated with the approach he suggests.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: If we took the approach that he suggests, we may only be able to afford to participate in one or two projects.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: And is that going to be the best approach for Singapore?

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: For Singapore to succeed, we must remain open.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Open to innovation, to talent, to data, to ideas from around the world.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: We will also need to work with partners from around the world to address the wide-ranging impact that AI can potentially have.
